The main reason for "tutorial hell" isn't a lack of discipline — it's decision fatigue. You spend more energy deciding WHAT to learn next than actually learning. To solve this for myself, I built a lightweight tool called SkillPilot: 👉 [ https://skillpath-ai-web-app-nwej.bolt.host ] How it works: You select or type your target goal (Full-Stack Dev, AI, Data Science, etc.). Input your current skill level and available weekly hours. It generates a single 5-stage action path telling you what to learn, what to build, and what to skip. It's 100% free with no account required.

articles.body: I wanted to build a portfolio that felt like something you'd actually explore, rather than another page with a photo, skills section, and a list of projects. So I turned my career into a small pixel-art world. Different islands represent different parts of my journey, with buildings and locations representing my education, work experience, projects, and other things I've built along the way. The idea The first version didn't work. I originally built a side-scrolling coastal town, but after spending time with it, I realized it wasn't communicating my experience clearly enough.
